shots.title: The Post-Interview Reality
shots.vo: Okay so. Imagine nailing a job interview, then finding out it pays less than your part-time gig at the chip shop.

shots.title: Mandatory *Salary Ranges*
shots.sub: UK moves to force pay transparency in job ads
shots.vo: Britain is reportedly moving to end that: salary ranges in job ads, mandatory.

shots.title: Expected vs Reality
shots.vo: Sounds like a pure win for workers. Here's the weird part: some research says rules like this might not raise average pay at all.

shots.title: Sneaky Economics
shots.sub: Why open salaries don't automatically mean bigger checks
shots.vo: And the reason is sneaky.

shots.title: *'Competitive'* Salary
shots.vo: Ground floor. Plenty of UK job ads just say 'competitive salary.' Competitive with what?

shots.title: The Job Market Stall
shots.vo: It's like a market stall with no price tags. You ask how much, and the seller looks you up and down: 'How much you got?'

shots.title: Information Asymmetry
shots.vo: The company has seen hundreds of salaries. You've seen yours. Economists call that information asymmetry.

shots.title: Pay Transparency Rollout
shots.vo: Britain isn't first: Colorado required pay ranges in postings from 2021, then New York City, California and Washington. The EU passed its own pay transparency directive in 2023.

shots.label: Staff Threshold
shots.sub: UK gender pay gap reporting since 2017
shots.vo: Nerd bonus: since 2017, UK employers with 250 or more staff have had to publish their gender pay gap every year.

shots.title: The Next Evolution
shots.vo: This is the next level: the price tag upfront.

shots.title: Same Job, Unequal Start
shots.vo: Meet Priya, a made-up graduate. Before the law, Company A offers her twenty-six grand. No idea if that's good, so she says yes.

shots.title: The Confidence Premium
shots.vo: The guy hired last month asked for more and got thirty. Same job. Different confidence.

shots.title: Mandated Range Posted
shots.vo: Now switch the law on. The ad says twenty-eight to thirty-two thousand. Priya knows the floor, and that asking for thirty is normal, not cheeky.

shots.title: Light On, Gap Shrinks
shots.sub: Pay gaps hide in who felt allowed to ask
shots.vo: Multiply that by millions of applicants. Pay gaps often hide in the dark, in who felt allowed to ask. Light on, gap shrinks.

shots.title: Episode *Over?*
shots.vo: Easy. Episode over. Thanks for watching.

shots.title: Ridiculous Ad Range
shots.vo: Except... why do some ads reportedly post ranges so wide they're useless? Like 'fifty thousand to half a million'? Hold that thought.

shots.label: Average Wage Impact
shots.vo: But here's the catch. Economists Zoe Cullen and Bobak Pakzad-Hurson studied US laws protecting workers' right to share their pay. Their headline finding: average wages fell, roughly two percent.

shots.title: The Unintended Twist
shots.vo: Wait, what?

shots.title: The Transparency Trap
shots.vo: Think like a boss. Give one hire a bigger offer, everyone sees it, everyone wants it. Every raise for one person quietly costs a raise for everyone.

shots.title: The Perfect Shield
shots.vo: So bosses get stubborn. 'Sorry, policy.' And because the policy's public, it's believable. Transparency gives companies a perfect excuse.

shots.title: Danish Pay Gap Compression
shots.label: Gap narrowed by slowing top-earner growth
shots.vo: So, the question from the start: does transparency raise average wages? Not reliably. What it does more consistently is squeeze pay together. A Danish study of gender pay reporting found the gap narrowed, reportedly mostly because men's wages grew more slowly.

shots.title: Compression Dynamics
shots.vo: Fairness achieved. By making the lads mildly sad.

shots.title: Why You Still Win
shots.vo: So what does this mean for you? Mostly good news. Students have the least insider info, so you gain the most. You can compare offers before sitting through three interview rounds.

shots.title: The Loophole
shots.vo: And loop two: those giant ranges are companies technically complying while telling you nothing. The legal minimum of honesty.

shots.title: Crucial Fine Print
shots.vo: Which is why the fine print matters: how wide a range is allowed and whether it must be a genuine number.

shots.title: The Tradeoff
shots.vo: Here's my take. Pay transparency is worth it. Not because it makes everyone richer, the evidence says it probably doesn't. Because it stops pay depending on who was brave or connected enough to ask. A fair game with smaller jackpots beats a rigged one.

shots.title: Realistic Progress
shots.vo: Back to the chip shop. This rule probably won't make your first salary huge. But you'll know it's small before the interview. Progress!

shots.label: Viral Negotiation Advice
shots.vo: And the most-viewed video on this topic right now is called 'Why You Should NEVER Negotiate Salary,' with over nine million views.

shots.title: Boss Perspective
shots.vo: With public ranges, your boss might be thinking the exact same thing.

shots.title: Money Moves
shots.sub: We read the price tag so you don't get ripped off.
shots.vo: Follow Money Moves. We read the price tag so you don't get ripped off.

shorts.title: Why Salary Transparency Actually Lowers Wages
